```{.quiz-yaml}
id: 03_central_tendency_grouped_mode
title: >
  Regrouping the same observations
questions:
  - id: total_observations
    type: numeric
    prompt: |
      Here are the same observations regrouped into bins 20 points wide instead
      of 10.

      | Score bin | $f$ |
      |--:|--:|
      | 0–19 | 8 |
      | 20–39 | 12 |
      | 40–59 | 28 |
      | 60–79 | 18 |
      | 80–99 | 7 |

      How many observations are represented in total? (i.e. what is the sample size, $n$?)
    hint: >
      Each observation belongs to exactly one bin. Add the frequencies in the
      $f$ column.
    answer: 73
    tolerance: 0
    explanation: >
      Each observation is counted once in one bin, so adding the frequencies
      gives $8 + 12 + 28 + 18 + 7 = 73$. Regrouping changes how the observations
      are arranged in the table, but it does not change how many there are. If
      we treat them as a sample, its sample size is $n = 73$.

  - id: compare_groupings
    type: multiple-choice
    prompt: >
      Which statement best compares this grouped table with [the original
      table](#tbl-grouped)?
    options:
      - text: The modal bin changes to 40–59, but the exact mode is still unknown
        correct: true
      - text: The modal bin remains 50–59 because the observations are unchanged
      - text: The exact mode is the score at the midpoint of 40–59
      - text: Every score from 40 through 59 occurred 28 times
    explanation: >
      Combining adjacent rows of the original table gives frequencies of 8, 12,
      28, 18, and 7. So with the wider bins, 40–59 is the modal bin. The
      underlying observations have not changed, only how they are grouped. And
      we still do not know how the 28 observations are divided among the exact
      scores from 40 through 59, so we cannot identify the exact mode.
```
